figures.caption: Lowest tested complete serving quotas across prompt lengths. Lines connect sampled points only; they do not identify an exact continuous physical frontier.
End-to-end architecture: concurrent request handling, common control interface, one worker, owned request state and measured feedback.
Request states and explicit unsuccessful outcomes. A rejection is different from worker failure, and neither is silently treated as a completed request.
Selective batching: dense work is shared while causal positions, histories and output ownership remain separate. Illustrative token counts are not measured data.
Precision transition and restoration lifecycle, including host masters, staging and temporary unpack scratch.
Placement and link traffic in the reference CPU-attention path. Migration differs from steady-state offloaded decode.
Separate memory pools and temporary lifetimes. The diagram is schematic and not to scale.
Validation-only one-block logit-KL sensitivity. Blocks 1, 7 and 9 form the selected three-block set.
A control tick with plan reuse, fresh feasibility, search, execution and explicit failure paths.
Separation of calibration, greedy serving, quality auditing and preserved experiment provenance.
Sampled training NLL for the actual 80-step tiny-decoder run. This demonstrates executable training, not general language capability.
Actual tiny-decoder resident storage and mean reference latency. Packed storage does not imply accelerated arithmetic.
